events.what: Doha talks between Iran and Qatari mediators produced a proposal that could reopen Hormuz within two days if a deal is reached with the US; no agreement finalized
Trump says Iran wants a deal and oil prices will go down a lot further; TD says part of risk premium priced out
ANZ: Gulf nations notified last week to prepare for a short, intense US military campaign; Trump has threatened to restart strikes after Nov. 3 midterms
At least seven vessel attacks Oct. 29-Nov. 2 incl. crude tankers Arzanah (Oct 29), Riti (Oct 30), LNG carrier Al Mayeda, first limpet-mine attack in years
Iranian state TV says tanker hit mines and caught fire east of Hormuz; IMO counted 30 attacks in Oct and urges ships to avoid the strait
Houthis claim missile strikes on Rabigh and Ras Tanura refineries and Abqaiq; Aramco gave no comment, no abnormal fires seen by NASA FIRMS
Atyrau-Samara crude flows suspended after Ukrainian drone attack on Samara hub; restart timing unclear
Zelenskyy: Ukraine will keep striking Russian refineries; strikes resumed Oct 30 after pause Oct 16-29; offers one-month pause for Patriot supply
Novak: diesel export ban to be extended to end-January with exceptions; November diesel export target about 2.15 million mt
Third US carrier strike group sent to Middle East; analysts see escalation risk during lame-duck period after the Nov. 3 midterms
UAE left OPEC and OPEC+ at end of April 2026
Asia-Pacific sweet crude trade on hold ahead of Nov. 3 US midterms

themes.summary: Futures fell to two-week lows and Dubai fell about 11% on Nov. 2 on hopes that Doha talks and Trump comments avert US-Iran escalation.

themes.theme: Hormuz attacks and post-midterm escalation risk
themes.summary: Seven vessel attacks since Oct. 29, Houthi claims on Saudi sites and warnings of strikes after Nov. 3 backstopped prices, with Goldman citing a risk premium near $27/b.

themes.theme: Eroded supply buffers and inventory draws
themes.summary: ADNOC says nearly 1 billion barrels drained from global stocks, SPR releases near zero and US crude stocks seen drawing a fifth week.
Vitol sees demand down 3 million b/d by end-2026, OPEC cut 2026 growth to 200,000 b/d, Japan imports fell 17.7% and Sinopec throughput fell 10.7%.
Ukraine resumed refinery strikes and hit the Samara hub halting Atyrau-Samara flows while ESPO loadings rose and NSR exports hit a record.

themes.theme: Asian buyers pay up for non-Hormuz barrels
themes.summary: Japan and South Korea record US and Americas crude imports, WTI Midland premiums reached $34.60/b on Sept. 18 and Oman Blend gains as a Hormuz bypass.

themes.theme: Atlantic Basin differentials at or near record lows
themes.summary: Europe is well supplied, CPC, Guyanese, Brazilian, WAF and North Sea grades weakened and Djeno hit an all-time low differential in October.
Suezmax index averaged $212,466.29/day in Q3 and Sinopec sees freight and insurance of $15/b or more in Q4, above $20/b in December.
